The area of rectangle A is 15 cm2.

parts.t: Write down the scale factor of the enlargement from A to B.
Work out the area of rectangle B.

sols: divide a length on B by the corresponding length on A
areas of similar shapes are in the ratio k2
Check: A is 5 by 3 and B is 15 by 9, giving 15 cm2 and 135 cm2 ✓

items.stem:
Triangle T and triangle U are mathematically similar.
Triangle T has area 20 cm2 and triangle U has area 45 cm2.

parts.t: Show that the length scale factor from T to U is 1.5.

The base of triangle T is 6 cm.
Work out the length of the base of triangle U.

sols: divide the larger area by the smaller area

items.stem:
Two solid prisms are mathematically similar.
The smaller prism has length 6 cm and the larger prism has length 15 cm.
The volume of the smaller prism is 48 cm3.

parts.t: Write down the length scale factor.
Calculate the volume of the larger prism.

sols: The prisms are similar, so all corresponding lengths are in the same ratio.
volumes of similar solids are in the ratio k3

items.stem:
Two solid statues are mathematically similar and are made from the same metal.
The smaller statue has height 15 cm and the larger statue has height 24 cm.
The mass of the smaller statue is 2.5 kg and its total surface area is 550 cm2.

parts.t: Write down the length scale factor.
Calculate the mass of the larger statue.
Calculate the total surface area of the larger statue.

sols: The statues are made of the same metal, so mass is proportional to volume.

items.stem:
Two jugs are mathematically similar.
The smaller jug holds 500 ml and the larger jug holds 1687.5 ml.

parts.t: Show that the length scale factor from the smaller jug to the larger jug is 1.5.

The height of the larger jug is 21 cm.
Work out the height of the smaller jug.

The surface area of the larger jug is 630 cm2.
Work out the surface area of the smaller jug.

sols: capacities of similar solids are in the ratio k3
divide by k to go from the larger to the smaller

items.stem:
In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC, and DE is parallel to BC.
AD = 6 cm, DB = 4 cm and the area of triangle ABC is 75 cm2.

parts.t: Calculate the area of triangle ADE.
Work out the area of the trapezium DBCE.

ms:
M1 for length scale factor 6⁄10 = 0.6 oe
M1 for 75 × 0.62 or 75 × 0.36
A1 cao
sols: DE is parallel to BC, so triangles ADE and ABC are similar.
The trapezium is what is left when triangle ADE is removed from triangle ABC.

items.stem: Two spheres have surface areas 100 cm2 and 225 cm2.

parts.t:
Find the ratio of their radii.
Give your answer in the form a : b, where a and b are integers in their simplest form.

Find the ratio of their volumes.
Give your answer in the form a : b, where a and b are integers in their simplest form.

sols: the surface areas are in the ratio k2

items.stem:
A solid cone has height 12 cm and volume 480 cm3.
The cone is cut into two parts by a plane parallel to the base, half way up the cone.
The upper part is a small cone and the lower part is a frustum.

parts.t: Calculate the volume of the small cone.
Work out the volume of the frustum.
Write down the ratio  volume of small cone : volume of frustum, in its simplest form.

sols: The small cone and the whole cone are similar, with k = 6⁄12 = 1⁄2.
the cut is parallel to the base, half way up

items.stem:
Two solid cones are mathematically similar and are made from the same material.
The larger cone has mass 8.1 kg and the smaller cone has mass 2.4 kg.

parts.t: Show that the length scale factor from the larger cone to the smaller cone is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>.

The height of the larger cone is 30 cm.
Work out the height of the smaller cone.

The total surface area of the larger cone is 1260 cm2.
Calculate the total surface area of the smaller cone.

sols: Both cones are made of the same material, so the ratio of the masses equals the ratio of the volumes.
take the cube root of the volume factor

items.stem:
A container is in the shape of a cone with the point at the bottom.
The cone has height 24 cm and its volume is 1500 cm3.
The container holds water to a depth of 18 cm.

parts.t:
Calculate the volume of the water.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

More water is poured in until the container is exactly half full.
Calculate the new depth of the water.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for length scale factor 18⁄24 = 0.75 oe
M1 for 1500 × 0.753 or 1500 × 0.421875
A1 (632.8125)
sols: The water forms a cone that is similar to the whole container.
the surface of the water is parallel to the top
Half full means the volume of water is <sup>1500</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = 750 cm<sup>3</sup>.
the depth is more than half of 24, as expected

items.stem: Two mathematically similar photographs have corresponding lengths in the ratio 2 : 5.

parts.t: Write down the ratio of their areas.

Two mathematically similar solids also have corresponding lengths in the ratio 2 : 5.
Write down the ratio of their volumes.

sols: Areas of similar shapes are in the ratio (length ratio)<sup>2</sup>.
square each part of the ratio
Volumes of similar solids are in the ratio (length ratio)<sup>3</sup>.
cube each part of the ratio

items.stem:
All circles are mathematically similar.
Circle P has radius 4 cm and area 50.3 cm2 (correct to 3 significant figures).
Circle Q has radius 10 cm.

parts.t:
Use the scale factor from P to Q to work out the area of circle Q.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

items.stem:
A model of a fishing boat is made to a scale of 1 : 50.
The model is 24 cm long.

parts.t: Work out the length of the real boat. Give your answer in metres.

The fuel tank of the real boat holds 250 litres.
Work out how much the fuel tank of the model would hold.
Give your answer in millilitres.

ms:
M1 for 250 ÷ 503 or 250 ÷ 125 000 or 0.002 litres
A1 cao
sols: every length on the real boat is 50 times the model
volumes of similar solids are in the ratio k3

items.stem:
A photocopier enlarges a diagram so that the area of the diagram is doubled.
The enlarged diagram is mathematically similar to the original.

parts.t:
Work out the length scale factor of the enlargement.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: every length is multiplied by about 1.41, not by 2

items.stem: A cube has edge length 5 cm. A second cube has edge length 20% greater.

parts.t: Work out the percentage increase in the surface area.
Work out the percentage increase in the volume.

sols: A 20% increase in length is a length scale factor of 1.2.
surface areas are in the ratio k2

items.stem:
Two garden ornaments are mathematically similar. The smaller is 30 cm tall and the larger is 45 cm tall.
It takes 120 ml of paint to cover the surface of the smaller ornament.

parts.t: Write down the length scale factor from the smaller to the larger ornament.
Work out how much paint is needed to cover the surface of the larger ornament.

sols: The amount of paint is proportional to the surface area.
paint covers area, so use k2, not k3

items.stem:
Two solid ornaments are mathematically similar.
The smaller ornament has surface area 72 cm2 and volume 135 cm3.
The larger ornament has surface area 200 cm2.

parts.t: Show that the length scale factor from the smaller to the larger ornament is <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>.
Calculate the volume of the larger ornament.

sols: surface areas are in the ratio k2

items.stem:
A plan of a garden is drawn to a scale of 1 : 200.
On the plan the lawn has an area of 45 cm2.

parts.t: Work out the real area of the lawn. Give your answer in square metres.

A path in the garden is 7 m long.
Work out the length of the path on the plan.

ms:
M1 for 45 × 2002 or 1 800 000 cm2 or 1 cm2 represents 4 m2
A1 cao
sols: Length scale factor = 200, so area scale factor = 200<sup>2</sup> = 40 000
or: 1 cm on the plan is 2 m, so 1 cm<sup>2</sup> is 4 m<sup>2</sup>, and 45 × 4 = 180
divide by k to go from real to plan

items.stem:
Two cans of paint are mathematically similar. The small can is 8 cm tall and holds 240 ml. The large can is 12 cm tall.
The small can costs $1.20 and the large can costs $3.60.

parts.t: Work out how much paint the large can holds.
Which can is better value for money? Show your working.

ms:
M1 for a correct comparison, e.g. 1.20 ÷ 240 = 0.005 and 3.60 ÷ 810 = 0.00444… ($ per ml), or 810 ÷ 3.60 = 225 ml per $ and 240 ÷ 1.20 = 200 ml per $
A1 for large can with correct figures
FT their (a)
sols: capacity is a volume, so use k3
Small can: $1.20 for 240 ml, that is 1.20 ÷ 2.4 = $0.50 per 100 ml
Large can: $3.60 for 810 ml, that is 3.60 ÷ 8.1 = $0.444… per 100 ml
$0.444 < $0.50, so the large can is better value
less money for the same amount of paint; note the price is 3 times but the paint is 3.375 times

items.stem:
The Earth and the Moon can be modelled as spheres.
The radius of the Earth is 6370 km and the radius of the Moon is 1740 km.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of  surface area of the Earth⁄surface area of the Moon .
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the value of  volume of the Earth⁄volume of the Moon .
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: All spheres are similar. Length scale factor k = 6370⁄1740 = 3.6609…
surface areas are in the ratio k2
check: 4π(6370)<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4π(1740)<sup>2</sup> gives the same value, the 4π cancels ✓
about 49 Moons would fit inside the Earth by volume

items.stem:
ABCD is a trapezium with AB parallel to DC.
AB = 4 cm and DC = 10 cm. The diagonals meet at X.
The area of triangle AXB is 8 cm2.

parts.t:
Triangles AXB and CXD are similar.
Calculate the area of triangle CXD.
Calculate the area of triangle AXD.

ms:
M1 for XD = 2.5 × XB (or AX : XC = 2 : 5) and triangles AXB, AXD having the same height from A
A1 cao
sols: alternate angles between the parallel lines, and vertically opposite angles at X
corresponding sides are in the ratio k
Triangles AXB and AXD have the same perpendicular height from A onto the line BXD.
so their areas are in the ratio of their bases XB : XD
Check: area of BXC is also 20, and 8 + 50 + 20 + 20 = 98 = ½(4 + 10) × height with height 14 ✓

items.stem: Rectangle A measures 6 cm by 9 cm. Rectangle B measures 8 cm by 12 cm.

parts.t: Show that the two rectangles are mathematically similar.

Amir says, “The ratio of the areas is 6 : 8, which is 3 : 4.”
Explain why Amir is wrong and write down the correct ratio area of A : area of B in its simplest form.

ms: B1 for both ratios equal to <sup>4</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> oe (or 6 : 9 = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3)

B1 for stating that areas are in the ratio (length ratio)2, not the length ratio, or 54 and 96 seen
B1 for 9 : 16
sols: Both pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so the rectangles are similar with k = 4⁄3
3 : 4 is the ratio of the lengths. Areas of similar shapes are in the ratio of the lengths squared.

items.stem:
In triangle ABC, D lies on AB, E lies on AC and DE is parallel to BC.
AD = 6 cm and BC = 8 cm.
The area of triangle ADE : the area of trapezium DBCE = 9 : 16.

parts.t: Show that the length scale factor from triangle ADE to triangle ABC is 5⁄3.
Work out the length of DB.
Work out the length of DE.

ms:
M1 for area ADE : area ABC = 9 : (9 + 16) = 9 : 25
A1 for √(25⁄9) = 5⁄3 nfww
sols: Triangle ABC is made up of triangle ADE and the trapezium, so area ADE : area ABC = 9 : (9 + 16) = 9 : 25
the trapezium is the rest of the big triangle
The triangles are similar (DE parallel to BC), so k2 = 25⁄9
DE corresponds to BC, and going from the large triangle to the small one divides by k.

items.stem:
The diagram shows a frustum made by removing a small square-based pyramid from the top of a larger square-based pyramid, using a cut parallel to the base.
The base of the frustum is a square of side 12 cm, the top is a square of side 3 cm and the height of the frustum is 15 cm.
[The volume of a pyramid is 1⁄3 × base area × height.]

parts.t: Show that the height of the small pyramid that was removed is 5 cm.
Calculate the volume of the frustum.

ms:
M1 for k = 3⁄12 = 1⁄4 and h⁄h + 15 = 1⁄4 oe
A1 for 4h = h + 15 ⇒ h = 5 nfww
sols: The small pyramid and the whole pyramid are similar, with k = 3⁄12 = 1⁄4
the cut is parallel to the base
Let the small pyramid have height h. Then the whole pyramid has height h + 15, and h⁄h + 15 = 1⁄4

items.stem:
Two solid trophies are mathematically similar and are made from the same metal.
The small trophy is 10 cm tall and the large trophy is 15 cm tall.
The total mass of the two trophies is 3.5 kg.

parts.t: Calculate the mass of each trophy.

The surface area of the small trophy is 80 cm2.
Calculate the surface area of the large trophy.

ms:
M1 for k3 = 1.53 = 3.375
M1 for m + 3.375m = 3.5 oe (or 3.5 shared in the ratio 1 : 3.375 or 8 : 27)
A1 for 0.8
A1 for 2.7
sols: k = 15⁄10 = 1.5, so the volume (and mass) scale factor is 1.53 = 3.375
same metal, so mass is proportional to volume
Let the small trophy have mass m kg. Then the large trophy has mass 3.375m kg.
m = 3.5 ÷ 4.375 = 0.8, so the small trophy is 0.8 kg and the large trophy is 3.5 − 0.8 = 2.7 kg
surface areas are in the ratio k2
Surface area of the large trophy = 80 × 2.25 = 180 cm2
